words.gloss: those who would drink eagerly (out of feigned love)

ai.literal: Even if they resemble those who would drink eagerly, the friendship of those who lack good character, rather than increasing, decreasing is pleasant.
ai.translation: Even if they appear so affectionate that they could drink you up, the friendship of those devoid of character is better off dwindling than growing.
ai.modern: நம்மை விழுங்குவது போல் அன்பு காட்டுபவர்களாக இருந்தாலும், நற்பண்பு இல்லாதவர்களின் நட்பு வளர்வதை விடத் தேய்ந்து போவதே நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns us about the superficial affection of unprincipled people. The phrase 'பருகுவார் போலினும்' vividly describes those who act so intensely loving that they seem ready to 'drink you up' or consume you with affection. However, if these people lack basic moral character (பண்பிலார்), their friendship (கேண்மை) is dangerous. The poet advises that it is far better (இனிது) for such a relationship to gradually fade away (குன்றல்) rather than to grow and strengthen (பெருகலின்).

ai.literal: If there is gain, befriending; if it ceases, abandoning; the friendship of those who have no comparison, even if gained, even if lost, what is the use?
ai.translation: What does it matter whether we gain or lose the friendship of those incomparable people who befriend us only when there is gain and abandon us when it ceases?
ai.modern: பயன் கிடைக்கும்போது நட்புக்கொண்டு, பயன் இல்லாதபோது விலகிப்போகும் ஒப்பில்லாத சுயநலவாதிகளின் நட்பைப் பெறுவதனால் என்ன பயன்? அதனை இழப்பதனால் என்ன நஷ்டம்?
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the nature of fair-weather friends who seek association solely for their own benefit. The word 'uṟiṉ' means when there is profit or gain, and 'aṟiṉ' means when that profit ceases. The word 'ṅaru'um' (a variant of 'orū'um') means to abandon or distance oneself. Such people are described as 'oppilār'—incomparable in their extreme selfishness. The poet asks what difference it makes ('eṉ') whether we gain ('peṟiṉum') or lose ('iỻappiṉum') their friendship, as it is completely worthless in either case.

ai.literal: Friendship that weighs the gain, those who take what is received, and thieves, are equal.
ai.translation: A friendship that calculates only personal gain, those who associate with others only for payment, and thieves are all alike.
ai.modern: கிடைக்கும் லாபத்தை ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்கும் நட்பும், கைம்மாறு பெறுபவர்களும், திருடர்களும் சமமானவர்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares three types of people: a calculating friend who only values a relationship for what they can gain from it, those who offer companionship solely for material payment, and thieves. All three are driven purely by selfish motives and lack genuine affection or moral commitment. The poet warns that a friend who constantly weighs their profit is no better than a thief, as both seek to take from you without any real bond. Understanding this comparison helps us identify and avoid superficial, transactional relationships.

words.gloss: than the companionship of such associates

ai.literal: In the midst of battle, on the way, abandoning, like an untrained horse, those who are like—than their companionship, solitude is best.
ai.translation: Solitude is far better than the companionship of those who, like an untrained horse, abandon their rider in the midst of battle.
ai.modern: போர்க்களத்தின் நடுவே தன் மேல் ஏறியவனைத் தள்ளிவிட்டு ஓடும் பழக்கப்படாத குதிரையைப் போன்றவர்களின் நட்பை விட, தனியாக இருப்பதே மிகச் சிறந்தது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns us against unreliable and harmful friends by comparing them to an untrained horse (கல்லாமா). Just as a wild, untrained horse will panic and throw its rider off in the middle of a battle (அமரகத்து ஆற்றறுக்கும்), bad friends will desert you when you face critical danger or adversity. The poet emphasizes that being completely alone (தனிமை) is far superior (தலை) to having the companionship of such untrustworthy people (தமரின்). The vivid imagery of the battlefield highlights how dangerous it is to rely on false friends during times of crisis.

ai.literal: Having made protection, not yielding, of mean people, the worthless friendship, than obtaining, not obtaining is good.
ai.translation: Rather than acquiring the worthless friendship of mean people, which does not yield any protection even when cultivated, it is far better not to acquire it at all.
ai.modern: பாதுகாப்பைத் தராத கீழ் குணமுடையவர்களின் தீய நட்பைப் பெறுவதை விட, அதனைப் பெறாமல் இருப்பதே நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the futility of forming alliances with base or mean-minded individuals. The poet describes their relationship as 'புன்கேண்மை' (worthless friendship) because, even if one puts effort into cultivating it, it fails to provide any safety or support ('ஏமம் சாரா') when needed. Therefore, the couplet concludes that not acquiring ('எய்தாமை') such a friendship is far better ('நன்று') than acquiring ('எய்தலின்') it, as it only brings vulnerability instead of security.

ai.literal: Than the highly intimate friendship of a fool, the estrangement of those who have wisdom is ten million times better.
ai.translation: Rather than the highly intimate friendship of a fool, the complete estrangement of wise people is ten million times better.
ai.modern: ஒரு பேதையின் மிக நெருக்கமான நட்பை விட, அறிவுடையவர்களின் பகைமை அல்லது விலகியிருக்கும் தன்மை கோடி மடங்கு மேலானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the close friendship of an ignorant person with the complete estrangement of wise people. The word 'பேதை' refers to a fool whose intense intimacy ('பெருங்கெழீஇ நட்பு') is unstable and dangerous. On the other hand, 'ஏதின்மை' refers to being strangers or having no relationship. The poet asserts that having no connection with wise people ('அறிவுடையார்') is ten million ('கோடி') times better ('உறும்') than being close to a fool, because even the indifference of the wise does no harm, whereas the friendship of a fool is inherently ruinous.

words.gloss: those whose nature is only laughter and amusement

ai.literal: Than the friendship of those who are of the nature of laughter only, from enemies ten multiplied by crore benefits will accrue.
ai.translation: Rather than the friendship of those who only make merry with you, ten million times more benefit will come from open enemies.
ai.modern: சிரித்துப் பேசிப் பொழுதுபோக்கும் தன்மையுடையவரின் நட்பை விட, பகைவர்களால் பத்து கோடி மடங்கு நன்மைகள் உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts superficial friends with open enemies. The term 'nakai-vakaiyar' refers to people whose association is limited to laughter, jokes, and superficial pleasantries, offering no genuine support in times of adversity. The poet declares that even the hostility of declared enemies is ten crore times more beneficial than such empty friendship. An open enemy allows one to be cautious and prepared, whereas a superficial friend gives a false sense of security and fails when help is most needed.

ai.literal: The friendship of those who obstruct a possible task, without speaking, let it slacken and abandon.
ai.translation: One should quietly let go of the friendship of those who obstruct or delay a task that is easily possible, without even speaking or arguing with them.
ai.modern: செய்யக்கூடிய செயலைச் செய்யவிடாமல் தடுப்பவர்களுடைய நட்பை, அவர்களிடம் எதுவும் பேசாமல் மெதுவாக நழுவவிட்டு விலக்கிவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on how to distance oneself from harmful friends who actively hinder or delay tasks that are otherwise easily achievable. The word 'உடற்றுபவர்' refers to those who obstruct or cause distress, while 'கேண்மை' means friendship. Instead of confronting or arguing with such people, which might lead to unnecessary conflict, the poet suggests letting the relationship quietly slip away ('சோர விடல்') without saying a word ('சொல்லாடார்'). This silent and gradual withdrawal is the safest way to end a toxic association.

ai.literal: Even in a dream, is unpleasant indeed, the friendship of those who have differed in action and differed in word.
ai.translation: Even in a dream, friendship with those whose deeds differ from their words is bitter.
ai.modern: செய்யும் செயல் வேறாகவும், சொல்லும் சொல் வேறாகவும் இருப்பவர்களுடைய நட்பு, கனவிலும் துன்பத்தைத் தருவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns us against hypocritical friends whose actions do not match their words. The key phrase 'வினைவேறு சொல்வேறு பட்டார்' describes deceitful people who say one thing but do another. The poet emphasizes that their friendship ('தொடர்பு') is painful ('இன்னாது') not just in waking life, but even in a dream ('கனவினும்'). The emphatic particle 'மன்னோ' highlights how deeply harmful and undesirable such deceptive relationships truly are.

ai.literal: Even in the least, approaching avoid, of those who are intimate at home but in public slander, the friendship.
ai.translation: Avoid even the slightest closeness with the friendship of those who act intimately in private but slander you in public.
ai.modern: வீட்டில் நெருக்கமாகப் பழகிவிட்டு, பொது அவையில் நம்மைப் பழித்துப் பேசுபவர்களின் நட்பை எவ்வளவும் நெருங்காமல் தவிர்த்தல் வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns us against hypocritical friends. The poet advises us to completely avoid (ஓம்பல்) even the slightest closeness (எனைத்தும் குறுகுதல்) with people who behave with great intimacy inside our homes (மனைக்கு எழீஇ) but speak ill of us or slander us in public assemblies (மன்றில் பழிப்பார்). The contrast between the private space of the home and the public space of the assembly highlights their deceitful nature. True friendship cannot coexist with such double standards, and keeping any connection with them is dangerous.
